title: Score Functions
story: Your teacher just graded 200 exams by hand — and made mistakes on five of them. You build an automatic grading system that never gets tired, never makes errors, and works instantly.
why: Conditional logic inside functions is a powerful pattern. Functions can make decisions (if/elif/else) and return different results based on input.
analogy: A grading function is like a coin sorter — coins go in, and the machine routes each one to the right slot based on its value.
try_it: Add a `grade_comment` function that returns "Excellent!" for A, "Good job!" for B, "Keep trying!" for C, and "Study more!" for D/F. Have it call `letter_grade` inside.
tips: Check the highest threshold first in `if/elif` chains: `>= 90` before `>= 80`
Use `else` as the final fallback — it catches everything that didn't match earlier conditions
Return a `Str` for categorical results and `Bool` for yes/no results — match the return type to the question
common_mistakes: Ordering `if/elif` from low to high — `if >= 60` first catches ALL passing grades before the higher checks run
Using `if` when you should use `else if` — each `if` is independent, so multiple can trigger
Forgetting the final `else` — what if someone enters a negative score? Handle it gracefully
